visuals.heading: Real Question After an MA

items.text: "What do I do with an MA" is not really about the subject anymore.
Compare by runway and risk first, subject and pay second.
Do not pick a door by prestige or by what a relative did.
Academia and civil services both ask for years of low or no income before any payoff.
A PhD without a guaranteed post, or a UPSC attempt with a roughly 0.1% overall selection ratio, both carry a genuine chance of no payoff after years of effort.
Many MA graduates run a corporate or teaching job while preparing for NET or a State PSC exam in parallel.
History, political science, sociology, and public administration optionals genuinely overlap with the syllabus.
A completed PhD funded by JRF, ICSSR, or another fellowship is a real credential, but permanent assistant professor vacancies open on their own schedule, not on your graduation date.

items.text: A PhD is always a safe, respectable choice.
Teaching is the fallback if nothing else works.
Government job or bust, private jobs are a downgrade.

blocks.heading: SSC, Banking, and PSU Exams Beyond UPSC

items.text: SSC CGL: opens central government roles across ministries and departments (Assistant, Inspector, and similar grades) to any postgraduate, with a shorter, more predictable prep cycle than UPSC CSE.

Bank PO and specialist officer exams (IBPS PO, SBI PO, RBI Grade B): accept any postgraduate degree, pay a structured, rising salary from day one, and generally have better odds than UPSC CSE, though still competitive.
PSU recruitment through non-technical hiring tracks: several public-sector undertakings run their own postgraduate-eligible drives for roles such as HR, corporate communications, and administration.
State-level Group B/C exams: often overlooked next to UPSC and the flagship State PSC exam, but genuinely faster to a paycheck and open to any MA subject.

blocks.heading: Sit One Real Past NET or UPSC

items.text: Ask one person already inside your target door, a JRF scholar, a PGT teacher, a State PSC officer, or a corporate hire in your field, what an ordinary week actually looks like, not the highlight-reel version.
Apply for one real opening in the corporate or teaching lane even while academia or civil services stays your first choice, so you have live market feedback instead of a theory.
